implementation_notes: Hand-write the pair for application state: keep a reference to the current snapshot, build the next one privately, then publish it with `Interlocked.Exchange(ref _current, finished)`, which 'sets a variable to a specified value as an atomic operation' and returns the previous frame for retirement. Readers use `Volatile.Read(ref _current)` (a reference read is atomic in any case) and then work on the snapshot without a lock. If the snapshots are genuinely immutable (records, `IReadOnlyList`) this is the whole pattern; if the buffer is a mutable array the writer keeps editing after publication, the pattern is defeated - the swap must be the last write to that generation.
pitfalls: `Interlocked.Exchange` publishes the reference only; keep editing the buffer afterwards and readers see torn data.
`Volatile.Read`/`Write` provide visibility, not atomicity of several fields - swap one reference, not a set of related fields.
In async code a `Task` handoff is usually clearer when the consumer must wait for the next frame; the swap is for 'latest version wins' only.

variants.name: WinForms OptimizedDoubleBuffer control drawing
variants.implementation_notes: On the rendering path the framework owns the pair: with `ControlStyles.OptimizedDoubleBuffer` the control 'is first drawn to a buffer rather than directly to the screen' and the finished buffer is blitted, which 'can reduce flicker' caused by incremental drawing; the documented combination also sets `UserPaint` and `AllPaintingInWmPaint`. WPF never exposes the buffer at all - it composites a retained scene offscreen. Use this variant when the buffered state is a control's visual output, and the snapshot swap above for non-UI state.
pitfalls: `OptimizedDoubleBuffer` alone is not enough: without `AllPaintingInWmPaint` the separate erase-background pass still flickers.
Repaints must be driven by `Invalidate`/`Refresh`; drawing from elsewhere bypasses the buffered path.
Controls with transparency or overlapping siblings can reintroduce flicker regardless of the style bits.
